analysis.title: We're Not in Kansas Anymore: Violent Rotation, but Not a Durable Bottom
key_insights: Rotation is violent beneath the surface. On Thursday and Friday five sectors gained more than 2% while two sectors lost more than 5%, and VIX has not yet closed above 20 despite the selloff in tech.
BTIG does not expect the volatility to end with a sub-20 VIX and expects correlations to rise on the downside.
SPX risk is to the 200 DMA, around 7300, which is also the June-July lows. SPX did not break its September lows, which BTIG reads as a sign a full washout has not happened yet.

Equal-weight semis (XSD) are on their second trip below the 200 DMA and nearing a third test of the July lows. SOXX is below its 200 DMA, and further weakness would break a six-month trading range to the downside. BTIG sees longer-term downside to the April breakout point ($365-400).
SOXX is down four weeks in a row, so counter-trend rallies are likely even though BTIG still sees meaningful downside in semis.
QQQ came close to its 200 DMA on Friday. BTIG expects a test and more likely an undercut toward the July lows.
NDX made a new all-time high in October but closed below September's low, a negative outside month. It is the first at an all-time high since September 2021 and the eighth since 1985.

In all seven prior NDX negative outside months at an all-time high, returns were positive six months later, but all seven also saw a drawdown of at least 8.5% in that window, and two (1990, 2020) saw 20% or more.
Sentiment is not washed out. Nasdaq DSI closed at 44, the lowest since July, versus lows of 30 in July and 12 in March.
There has been no NYSE day with 80%+ downside volume in nearly a year, which BTIG calls unprecedented. BTIG wants to see at least one, if not several, before playing offense.

Credit is weakening up the quality ladder. Average HY spreads hit 340bps, the YTD wides and the widest since spring 2025, after earlier weakness was limited to CCCs. IG tech spreads are nearing the 2022 wides.
Staples gained over 11% in October, their best month since October 2000, which BTIG reads as a flight to safety.
Healthcare (XLV) is 16.5% above its 200 DMA, essentially tying the widest spread in its history. BTIG sees it as a likely candidate for an unwind in a correlation-one selloff or an AI rebound.
Utilities (XLU) rallied 11% into key resistance after BTIG liked them in September. BTIG says the risk/reward has flipped.
Gold broke its summer lows, completing a topping pattern, and BTIG sees downside toward $3500/oz. Silver shows weakness with downside toward $40/oz.

Polling and betting markets put the odds of a Democrat winning the Kansas Senate race above 50%. Kansas has not gone blue in the Senate since 1932. BTIG has no view on the outcome and notes polls are often wrong.

A blue sweep would in theory be a headwind for the data center build-out. BTIG still thinks the midterms are not a clearing event for the broad market, but would cover tactical AI shorts if semis and AI fall further into Tuesday evening.
